newsitem.title: UK: BA extends gains as Lufthansa deal takes off.
newsitem.headline: BA extends gains as Lufthansa deal takes off.

text.p: Shares in British Airways Plc extended early gains after Deutsche Lufthansa AG formally launched its new airline alliance with United Airlines, Star Alliance, analysts said.
BA traded at a fresh record high of 741-1/2p, 30p up, by 1308 GMT, and was up about 25p at midday.
"People will be saying, 'If that is allowed then why shouldn't the BA-American alliance go through?'," said one analyst.
"That's causing a little more interest in the stock," he said.
Nearly a year ago BA and American Airlines revealed their alliance but their deal is still enmeshed in a complex web of regulatory processes.

The Lufthansa-United tie-up obtained immunity from U.S. anti-trust laws before the BA-American deal was floated, and BA has always cited this as a precendent for why it should be allowed to link up with American.

Lufthansa said its alliance, which includes United Airlines, Air Canada, Scandinavian Airlines Systems and Thai Airways International Ltd, would also add Brazil's Varig Airlines but there would be no merger.
BA shares rose earlier after a "split" order - where a customer deals through different brokers - met a shortage of stock and a consequent price squeeze.

Dealers and analysts said the stock was boosted also by upbeat bookings comment and results from Airtours Plc and indications from American on Tuesday that it expected news from the new British government within the next two weeks on the proposed BA alliance.
